[Thinking]
**Exploring Frequency Analysis**

My current focus is on translating the ultrasound signal from the time domain to the frequency domain. I'm deep in the process of considering how best to represent this spectral information, specifically looking at magnitude in dB versus frequency.

**Analyzing Spectral Representation**

I am currently refining the frequency domain representation. My thoughts are centered on how best to scale the FFT output and converting the magnitude to decibels for optimal visualization and analysis against frequency.

**Refining Frequency Scaling**

I'm now concentrating on the precise scaling of the frequency axis. My aim is to ensure the representation in MHz accurately reflects the spectral content after the FFT and magnitude calculations.
[/Thinking]

Here is a complete MATLAB program to convert an ultrasound time-domain signal into a frequency-domain spectrum. 

Since you will likely be importing your own data, I have divided the code into two sections. The first section generates a synthetic ultrasound pulse (so you can run the code immediately to see how it works). The second section is the actual processing algorithm you will use.

```matlab
%% SECTION 1: Generate Synthetic Ultrasound Signal
% (Replace this section with your own data loading code, e.g., readmatrix or load)

fs = 50e6;                  % Sampling rate (50 MHz)
dt = 1/fs;                  % Time step
t = 0:dt:10e-6;             % Time vector (from 0 to 10 microseconds)

% Create a synthetic 5 MHz Gaussian-modulated ultrasound pulse
fc = 5e6;                   % Center frequency of 5 MHz
voltage = exp(-((t-5e-6)/0.5e-6).^2) .* sin(2*pi*fc*t); 

%% SECTION 2: Signal Processing (Voltage-Time to Magnitude-Frequency)

% 1. Extract sampling information from the time vector
L = length(t);              % Length of the signal
Ts = t(2) - t(1);           % Sampling period (seconds)
Fs = 1/Ts;                  % Sampling frequency (Hz)

% 2. Perform the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
V_fft = fft(voltage);

% 3. Calculate the two-sided spectrum, then convert to single-sided
P2 = abs(V_fft / L);                % Two-sided magnitude
P1 = P2(1:floor(L/2)+1);            % Keep only the positive frequencies
P1(2:end-1) = 2 * P1(2:end-1);      % Multiply by 2 to conserve energy (except DC and Nyquist)

% 4. Convert Magnitude to Decibels (dB)
% Add 'eps' (a very small number) to prevent log10(0) returning negative infinity
mag_dB = 20 * log10(P1 + eps); 

% 5. Create the Frequency Vector and convert to MHz
f_Hz = Fs * (0:(L/2)) / L;          % Frequency axis in Hz
f_MHz = f_Hz / 1e6;                 % Convert Frequency to MHz

%% SECTION 3: Plotting the Results

figure('Name', 'Ultrasound Signal Analysis', 'Position', [100, 100, 800, 600]);

% Plot 1: Time Domain (Voltage vs Time)
subplot(2,1,1);
plot(t * 1e6, voltage, 'b', 'LineWidth', 1.5); % Time converted to microseconds for easier reading
grid on;
title('Time Domain: Ultrasound Signal');
xlabel('Time (\mu s)');
ylabel('Voltage (V)');

% Plot 2: Frequency Domain (Magnitude(dB) vs Frequency(MHz))
subplot(2,1,2);
plot(f_MHz, mag_dB, 'r', 'LineWidth', 1.5);
grid on;
title('Frequency Domain: Amplitude Spectrum');
xlabel('Frequency (MHz)');
ylabel('Magnitude (dB)');
xlim([0, 15]); % Limit x-axis to 15 MHz for better visibility of the 5 MHz pulse
```

### How to use this with your own data:
1. Delete or comment out **Section 1**.
2. Load your data. If your data is in an Excel or CSV file, you can load it like this:
   ```matlab
   data = readmatrix('my_ultrasound_data.csv');
   t = data(:, 1);       % Assuming 1st column is Time (in seconds)
   voltage = data(:, 2); % Assuming 2nd column is Voltage
   ```
3. Run the rest of the script. The code automatically calculates the sampling frequency based on your time vector.
